# Entity commands: find, get, create, update, delete, revive

## `fptctl create`

Create an entity of TYPE.

TYPE is an entity type. Give field values with --set (repeatable): FIELD=TEXT sets a string, and FIELD:=JSON sets a typed value such as a number, a list or an entity link. --data gives all the fields as one JSON object, and --set wins over --data. Prints the new entity.

```text
fptctl create [OPTIONS] TYPE
```

Library call: `Shotgun.create`.

Options:

- `--set FIELD=TEXT|FIELD:=JSON`: A field value; repeatable. '=' gives text, ':=' gives typed JSON.
- `--data JSON|@FILE|-`: All fields as an object.
- `--return-fields A,B`: Fields to return besides those set.
- `--dry-run`: Print the library call instead of making it.

Examples:

```shell
fptctl create Shot --set code=sh010 --set 'project:={"type": "Project", "id": 70}'
fptctl create Asset --data '{"code":"chair","project":{"type":"Project","id":70}}' --dry-run
```

## `fptctl delete`

Retire (soft-delete) entity ID of TYPE.

TYPE is an entity type and ID the entity's id. A retired entity can be brought back with revive. On a terminal, delete asks for confirmation; anywhere else it needs --yes. Prints true when the entity was retired.

```text
fptctl delete [OPTIONS] TYPE ID
```

Library call: `Shotgun.delete`.

Options:

- `--yes`: Do not ask for confirmation.
- `--dry-run`: Print the library call instead of making it.

Examples:

```shell
fptctl delete Shot 1234 --yes
fptctl delete Shot 1234 --dry-run
```

## `fptctl find`

Find entities of TYPE.

TYPE is an entity type, such as Shot or Asset. Filter with -f (repeatable and ANDed; --any ORs them), or pass the raw API filter structure with --filters. With no --limit every match comes back, and with no --fields the library's default fields. Prints a list of entities.

```text
fptctl find [OPTIONS] TYPE
```

Library call: `Shotgun.find`.

Options:

- `-f, --filter 'FIELD OP VALUE'`: A condition; repeat to AND them. VALUE is JSON, Type:123, or text.
- `--any`: Match any condition instead of all.
- `--filters JSON|@FILE|-`: The raw filter structure; not with -f.
- `--fields A,B`: Fields to return.
- `--order A,-B`: Sort fields; '-' for descending.
- `--limit INTEGER`: Return at most N entities (default: every match).
- `--page INTEGER`: Return page N of --limit entities.
- `--retired-only`: Return only retired (deleted) entities.
- `--include-archived-projects true|false`: Include entities in archived projects (the library default is true).
- `--additional-filter-presets JSON|@FILE|-`: Filter presets.

Examples:

```shell
fptctl find Shot -f 'project is Project:70' --fields code,sg_status_list
fptctl find Shot -f 'sg_status_list in ["ip","rev"]' --order -created_at --limit 10
fptctl find Version --filters '[["code", "contains", "v001"]]' --limit 50 --page 2
```

## `fptctl get`

Get one entity of TYPE by ID.

TYPE is an entity type and ID the entity's id. Prints the entity, or null with exit 0 when there is none, exactly as the library's find_one returns it. With --must-exist a missing entity exits 4 instead.

```text
fptctl get [OPTIONS] TYPE ID
```

Library call: `Shotgun.find_one`.

Options:

- `--fields A,B`: Fields to return.
- `--order A,-B`: Sort fields; '-' for descending.
- `--any`: Send filter_operator 'any'.
- `--retired-only`: Return only retired (deleted) entities.
- `--include-archived-projects true|false`: Include entities in archived projects (the library default is true).
- `--additional-filter-presets JSON|@FILE|-`: Filter presets.
- `--must-exist`: Exit 4 if there is no such entity.

Examples:

```shell
fptctl get Shot 1234 --fields code,sg_status_list
fptctl get Shot 1234 --must-exist
```

## `fptctl revive`

Revive a retired entity ID of TYPE.

TYPE is an entity type and ID the id of an entity that delete retired. Prints true when the entity was revived.

```text
fptctl revive [OPTIONS] TYPE ID
```

Library call: `Shotgun.revive`.

Options:

- `--dry-run`: Print the library call instead of making it.

Examples:

```shell
fptctl revive Shot 1234
```

## `fptctl update`

Update entity ID of TYPE.

TYPE is an entity type and ID the entity's id. Field values work as for create: --set FIELD=TEXT, --set FIELD:=JSON, or --data. --multi-entity-mode chooses whether a multi-entity field's list is replaced (set), added to (add) or removed from (remove). Prints the updated fields.

```text
fptctl update [OPTIONS] TYPE ID
```

Library call: `Shotgun.update`.

Options:

- `--set FIELD=TEXT|FIELD:=JSON`: A field value; repeatable. '=' gives text, ':=' gives typed JSON.
- `--data JSON|@FILE|-`: All fields as an object.
- `--multi-entity-mode FIELD=set|add|remove`: How a multi-entity field is changed; repeatable. The library default is set.
- `--dry-run`: Print the library call instead of making it.

Examples:

```shell
fptctl update Shot 1234 --set sg_status_list=ip --set sg_cut_in:=1001
fptctl update Shot 12 --set 'assets:=[{"type":"Asset","id":7}]' --multi-entity-mode assets=add
```
